OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C2 communication to FireAnt-campaign domains/IPs AICommand & Control Medium
Alerts on host connections or DNS lookups to the SPECTRALVIPER command-and-control domains and IPs used across the FireAnt MetaKit and construction-firm intrusions (2024-2026). Article-specific: every indicator is a confirmed campaign C2 from the ESET report and Table 2. Rationale: Uses the confirmed SPECTRALVIPER C2 domains (financemachinelearning.com etc. from Table 2) and the resolved IPs; multiple second sources (Elastic, ESET, CyberSecurityNews) attribute these to the same campaign, so no single-source-only IOCs were shipped. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/oceanlotus-hits-vietnam-investors-with.html • https://www.scworld.com/brief/oceanlotus-targets-stock-investors-and-construction-firm-with-spectralviper-backdoor
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel/IOC scanners or TIP enrichment jobs resolving the domains for validation
  • Sinkholed domains post-takedown resolving to a research sinkhole IP
  • A shared-hosting IP later reassigned to a benign tenant (IP clause stale)
  • Security researcher detonating samples on a corporate analysis subnet
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("MsSense.exe","SenseIR.exe","MsMpEng.exe") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "Windows Defender")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the InitiatingProcessFileName making the connection — OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe, IntelAudioService.exe, setup.exe or an unexpected process strongly confirms SPECTRALVIPER; note whether the URL contains /apparatus/wind/twig/statement.html. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block the C2 domains/IPs at proxy and firewall, and revoke any cached creds from that host. 3) Hunt: sweep all hosts for the same destinations over 90 days, look for the DtlCrashCatch.dll side-load and setup.exe hashes, and check FireAnt MetaKit install footprint org-wide.

let c2IPs = dynamic(["139.162.11.152","142.91.98.77","139.180.128.42","139.99.33.239","166.88.77.186","103.119.47.104","38.60.245.37","194.68.26.241"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (c2IPs) or RemoteUrl has_any (c2Domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA1, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let c2Domains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);

(ImNetworkSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DstIpAddr in (c2IPs) | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, Src=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=DstIpAddr, IndicatorType="ip"),
(ImDnsActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DnsQuery has_any (c2Domains) | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, Src=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=DnsQuery, IndicatorType="domain")

FireAnt MetaKit trojanized setup.exe (SPECTRALVIPER downloader) by known hash AIDelivery High
Alerts on execution of the trojanized FireAnt MetaKit installer (setup.exe) variants that delivered SPECTRALVIPER, matched on the 20 campaign SHA1 hashes. Targets the supply-chain delivery step rather than later C2, giving earliest-possible detection. Rationale: The 20 setup.exe SHA1 hashes are the article's pre-extracted IOC list, corroborated by CyberSecurityNews as the FireAnt MetaKit SPECTRALVIPER downloader variants; hash equality is exact and zero-FP outside the campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/oceanlotus-apt-compromises-fireant-metakit/ • https://gbhackers.com/oceanlotus-targets-stock-investors/ • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware sandbox/CI detonation hosts executing the collected samples
  • Security-team threat-hunt VM running the IOC for validation
  • EDR re-scan of a previously quarantined file generating a synthetic process record
  • Hash collision is cryptographically implausible for SHA1 here — no benign FP expected from the hash itself
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the host actually ran FireAnt MetaKit and capture parent process + user; verify the file path (was it served by the FireAnt updater?). 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill and quarantine the binary, and pull memory before reboot to capture the injected SPECTRALVIPER in OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe. 3) Hunt: enumerate all FireAnt MetaKit installs org-wide, search for the side-load DLL DtlCrashCatch.dll and connections to financemachinelearning.com, and scope which update versions were pulled in the Oct 2025-Mar 2026 window.

SPECTRALVIPER injected OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe beaconing (Cookie-header C2) AICommand & Control High
Hunts SPECTRALVIPER's post-injection beacon: the masqueraded OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe (injection target) making public outbound connections, or any host reaching the hardcoded beacon path /apparatus/wind/twig/statement.html. Catches the C2 stage even if domain/IP infrastructure rotates, by pivoting on the injected host process and unique URI. Rationale: Pivots on the named injection target OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe (cybersecuritynews) plus the hardcoded beacon URI /apparatus/wind/twig/statement.html — a legit OneDrive sync uses OneDrive.exe, so this process name reaching public C2 is high-fidelity and survives infrastructure rotation. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/oceanlotus-apt-compromises-fireant-metakit/ • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper
ATT&CKT1055 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A genuine third-party app legitimately named OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe (uncommon — real binary is OneDrive.exe) hitting a benign CDN
  • Web-proxy URL-decode artifacts matching the statement.html path on an unrelated site (the full /apparatus/wind/twig/ path makes this very unlikely)
  • Internal vuln scanner probing the beacon URI during an IOC sweep
  • Microsoft OneDrive telemetry endpoints if the host process name is spoofed but destination is legitimately Microsoft (excluded by C2 dest clause in proxy variant)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\OneDrive" and Dests has_any (dynamic(["13.107.42.12","13.107.6.171"])))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe path and signer — a real OneDrive sync process is OneDrive.exe under AppData\Local\Microsoft\OneDrive; an unsigned/oddly-pathed OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe with public egress is the injected SPECTRALVIPER. 2) Contain: isolate the host, capture a memory image to recover the injected payload, then block the C2 and kill the process. 3) Hunt: pivot the host for the DtlCrashCatch.dll side-load and setup.exe hashes, and search proxy logs org-wide for the /apparatus/wind/twig/statement.html URI and Cookie-header beacons to the campaign domains.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe" and RemoteIPType == "Public")
     or RemoteUrl has "/apparatus/wind/twig/statement.html"
| summarize ConnCount=count(), Dests=make_set(RemoteIP, 50), Urls=make_set(RemoteUrl, 50), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA1
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has "/apparatus/wind/twig/statement.html" or UrlOriginal has "apparatus/wind/twig/statement.html"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, Url, HttpUserAgent=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DstIpAddr, DstHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

| where RemoteIP in ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241") or RemoteUrl has_any ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
ImNetworkSession

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688

| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.

   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"

status: experimental
description: |

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when

    vendor.

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

CISA KEV: CVE-2026-10520 — Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Vulnerability

CISA KEV
2026-06-11 1 use case 1 technique 2 kill-chain phases detected

Ivanti Sentry (formerly known as MobileIron Sentry) contains an OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution. This vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable. The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors. Vendor: Ivanti, Product: Sentry. Federal patch due: 2026-06-14.

Malicious 'postmark-mcp' MCP server package present/executing on developer endpoints AIDelivery High
Hunts for the trojanised npm package postmark-mcp (backdoored at v1.0.16) landing in node_modules or being launched on a developer device. The malicious MCP server silently BCCs every outgoing email to phan@giftshop.club, so any presence of this exact package is a compromise indicator, not generic supply-chain noise. Rationale: Uses the exact malicious package name 'postmark-mcp' and its node_modules drop path named in the article ('first confirmed malicious MCP server ... blind-copying every outgoing email') — cross-checked against Koi Security, Snyk and The Hacker News, which confirm the v1.0.16 backdoor BCCing to phan@giftshop.club (the article IOC giftshop.club). Cross-checked against: • https://www.koi.ai/blog/postmark-mcp-npm-malicious-backdoor-email-theft • https://snyk.io/blog/malicious-mcp-server-on-npm-postmark-mcp-harvests-emails/ • https://thehackernews.com/2025/09/first-malicious-mcp-server-found.html • https://postmarkapp.com/blog/information-regarding-malicious-postmark-mcp-package
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1114 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A malware analyst or AppSec engineer detonating/reviewing the sample in an isolated sandbox VM
  • An internal mirror/cache (Verdaccio, Artifactory) retaining a quarantined copy of the package for forensic review
  • A blocklist test where the package is intentionally installed to validate Aikido/EDR detection
  • A developer who pinned the legitimate Postmark official SDK but typo-named a local wrapper folder 'postmark-mcp'
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("MALWARE-SANDBOX","SECLAB","DETONATION"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the installed version from package.json/package-lock on the host — any version >=1.0.16 is backdoored. Confirm the file write was under an interactive developer account, not a CI runner. 2) Contain: remove the package, kill any running node MCP process, and rotate the Postmark Server API token plus any credentials/secrets that transited email while it was installed. 3) Hunt: search mail logs for BCC recipients @giftshop.club, and sweep all developer endpoints for the same node_modules\postmark-mcp path to scope blast radius.
let lookback = 30d;
union
(DeviceProcessEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
 | where ProcessCommandLine has "postmark-mcp"
 | where AccountName !endswith "$"
 | extend Signal="process", Path=FolderPath, Cmd=ProcessCommandLine, Hash=SHA256),
(DeviceFileEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
 | where FolderPath has @"\node_modules\postmark-mcp"
 | extend Signal="file", Path=FolderPath, Cmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Hash=SHA256, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Signal, Path, Cmd, Hash
| order by Timestamp desc
let lookback = 30d;
union
(ImFileEvent
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
 | where TargetFilePath has @"\node_modules\postmark-mcp"
 | extend Signal="file", Path=TargetFilePath, Cmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash=TargetFileSHA256, User=ActorUsername),
(ImProcessCreate
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
 | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "postmark-mcp" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "postmark-mcp" or ParentProcessCommandLine has "postmark-mcp"
 | extend Signal="process", Path=TargetProcessName, Cmd=TargetProcessCommandLine, Hash=SHA256, User=ActorUsername)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, User, Signal, Path, Cmd, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects the trojanised postmark-mcp MCP server package (backdoored v1.0.16+) being written into a node_modules directory on a developer host. The package BCCs all outgoing email to phan@giftshop.club.
references:
  - https://www.koi.ai/blog/postmark-mcp-npm-malicious-backdoor-email-theft
  - https://snyk.io/blog/malicious-mcp-server-on-npm-postmark-mcp-harvests-emails/

tags:

  - attack.t1114

    TargetFilename|contains: '\node_modules\postmark-mcp\'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon ((@EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\node_modules\\postmark-mcp\\* OR *\\node_modules\\Postmark-Mcp\\*)) OR (@EventID:1 @CommandLine:*postmark-mcp*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\node_modules\\postmark-mcp\\/i

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` 
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` 
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` 
| sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*postmark-mcp*" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process 
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` 
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` 
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` 
| sort - lastTime
GlassWorm Stage-2 C2 beacon to Vultr-hosted command-and-control IPs AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts outbound connections from developer endpoints to GlassWorm's confirmed C2 infrastructure (Vultr IPs 45.32.150.251, 45.32.151.157, 70.34.242.255 and the payload/exfil host 217.69.3.152 serving /wall). GlassWorm backdoors VS Code / OpenVSX extensions, so the initiating process is typically Code.exe, an extension host, or node. Rationale: Pivots on GlassWorm's confirmed C2 IPs named in external write-ups (Koi/BleepingComputer/Truesec) — the article-provided IOCs 45.32.150.251, 45.32.151.157 and 70.34.242.255 are corroborated as Vultr C2, and 217.69.3.152/wall is the confirmed zipped-exfil endpoint. The article names the GlassWorm VS Code extension compromise explicitly. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/glassworm-botnet-disrupted-after-resilient-c2-infrastructure-takedown/ • https://www.truesec.com/hub/blog/glassworm-self-propagating-vscode-extension • https://www.veracode.com/blog/glassworm-vs-code-extension/ • https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/03/glassworm-attack-installs-fake-browser-extension-for-surveillance
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1195.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vultr is shared hosting — after the March 2026 takedown these IPs may be reassigned to a benign tenant, producing stale-IOC hits
  • A red-team / pentest engagement that happens to stand up infrastructure on the same Vultr ranges
  • A developer browsing to an unrelated site now hosted on a recycled IP
  • A threat-intel sandbox or VirusTotal retro-hunt VM detonating the sample and beaconing out
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the initiating process — GlassWorm beacons originate from Code.exe, the extension host, or node; a browser hitting the IP is far lower priority. Check whether the host has recently installed/updated VS Code or OpenVSX extensions. 2) Contain: isolate the endpoint, block the four C2 IPs at the egress firewall, and disable/remove suspect extensions. 3) Hunt: enumerate installed VS Code/OpenVSX extensions for invisible-Unicode payloads, search for the Solana-wallet C2-resolution traffic and connections to 217.69.3.152/wall, and check for credential/crypto-wallet file access across other developer hosts.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("45.32.150.251","45.32.151.157","70.34.242.255","217.69.3.152")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("45.32.150.251","45.32.151.157","70.34.242.255","217.69.3.152")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:

author: Clankerusecase

logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'

        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'

falsepositives:

      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or SHA1 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or MD5 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or SHA1 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or MD5 in~ ("2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

go-base forged-JWT auth bypass: Bearer access to /api/v1/admin & token/refresh routes AIExploitation Medium
Hunts exploitation of CVE-2026-48031, where an attacker forges an HS256 JWT signed with the public hardcoded secret "random" and presents it to dhax/go-base protected routes. Targets successful (2xx) requests carrying an Authorization: Bearer header to the boilerplate's fixed route set (/api/v1/admin/*, /api/v1/token/refresh, /api/v1/me), especially from non-browser clients like the PoC's python-requests. Rationale: Pivots on the dhax/go-base PoC's concrete route set (/api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/token/refresh, /api/v1/me) plus the Bearer header and PoC client UA (python-requests) — these paths are boilerplate-fixed so they are article-specific. defender_kql is empty: Defender Advanced Hunting has no web-access-log table, so this detection lives on proxy/IIS/ASIM web telemetry only. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm • https://dailycve.com/go-rest-api-boilerplate-go-base-hardcoded-jwt-secret-cwe-798-cve-2026-48031-critical-dc-jun2026-325/
ATT&CKT1606 T1078 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admins/operators calling /api/v1/admin/* from automation or scripts with python-requests/curl UA
  • Health-check or monitoring probes hitting /api/v1/me with a valid service-account token
  • CI/CD integration tests exercising the token/refresh endpoint
  • Internal API gateways that rewrite the User-Agent to a non-browser string
  • Mobile/SPA clients legitimately using Go-http-client or okhttp libraries
Suppression filter
| where not (SrcIpAddr in ("<known-monitoring-ips>")) // replace via watchlist; or restrict to external SrcIpAddr only: | where ipv4_is_private(SrcIpAddr) == false
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the SrcIpAddr and decode the JWT from the proxy log (if captured) — a forged token shows the hardcoded 'random' HS256 signature and absurd claims (iat/exp ~9999999000, roles:[admin]). Confirm whether the source IP/account ever performed a real /login or pwdless auth. 2) Contain: rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET to a 32+ char value (openssl rand -base64 32), redeploy to invalidate all existing tokens, and block the offending source IP at the WAF. 3) Hunt: review all 2xx /api/v1/admin/* and /api/v1/token/refresh hits over the retention window for the same IP/UA, and audit user/data-modifying API calls made with the forged identity.
let GoBasePaths = dynamic(["/api/v1/admin/","/api/v1/token/refresh","/api/v1/me"]);

CVE-2026-48031 exposure: assets running vulnerable dhax/go-base boilerplate AIExploitation High
Attack-surface hunt that surfaces hosts where Defender TVM has flagged CVE-2026-48031 (dhax/go-base hardcoded JWT secret), so the SOC can prioritise rotating AUTH_JWT_SECRET and upgrading past PR#31 (fixed commit cc82b9740fa6, May 17 2026) before forged-token bypass occurs. Rationale: Uses the concrete CVE id (CVE-2026-48031) and the article's patched commit/version boundary to enumerate exposed assets. Note coverage caveat: go-base is a compiled-in Go module/boilerplate, so TVM only fires where the inventory scanner attributes it — treat zero results as 'not inventoried', not 'not exposed'. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm • https://dailycve.com/go-rest-api-boilerplate-go-base-hardcoded-jwt-secret-cwe-798-cve-2026-48031-critical-dc-jun2026-325/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Lab/test hosts intentionally running unpatched go-base for research
  • Internal-only dev instances not reachable from untrusted networks (lower real risk despite CVE match)
  • Assets already remediated but TVM inventory not yet rescanned (stale finding)
  • Decommissioned hosts still present in the software inventory snapshot
Response runbook
1) Triage: for each flagged DeviceName, confirm the go-base service is running and internet-exposed; check whether AUTH_JWT_SECRET is still the default 'random' or another weak value. 2) Contain: rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET to a 32+ char secret and redeploy past fixed commit cc82b9740fa6 (PR#31); restart to invalidate any pre-existing forged tokens. 3) Hunt: cross-reference these hosts against UC1 web-log results for prior forged-token access to /api/v1/admin/* or /api/v1/token/refresh.

Exfiltration to attacker-controlled Sentry ingest endpoint (onering crate) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts outbound traffic to the specific Sentry org/project used by the trojanised onering 1.4.1 crate to disguise stolen git diffs as crash telemetry. The org id o4511539639222272 / project 4511539669368912 is attacker-controlled, so any contact is high-fidelity regardless of which package or build host triggered it. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact attacker Sentry infrastructure (host o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io, project 4511539669368912/envelope). This org/project id is attacker-owned, so a match is not generic Sentry crash reporting. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-rust-crate-onering-performs-code-exfiltration • https://intel.aikido.dev/malware • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/trapdoor-supply-chain-attack-spreads.html
ATT&CKT1567 T1071.001 T1036
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher reproducing the onering build inside a sandbox
  • EDR/CI detonation chamber building the crate for analysis
  • An internal app erroneously configured with this exact DSN (effectively impossible — org id is attacker-owned)
  • Legitimate Sentry telemetry to a DIFFERENT org/project (will not match this host)
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the host and the build that resolved the domain; confirm a Cargo build was running and pull Cargo.lock to see if onering 1.4.1 (or a git pin of cenotelie/onering) is present. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io at egress/DNS, and treat the most recent commit diff as exfiltrated — rotate any secrets that appeared in recent commits. 3) Hunt: sweep all dev/CI hosts for the same domain and for onering 1.4.1 in lockfiles; review git history for what diffs would have leaked.

Rust build script harvesting git commit diff (onering build.rs) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the onering build.rs collection step: a Rust build-script-build.exe spawning git to capture the latest commit's full diff and metadata. Anchored on the exact `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` and the malicious `--pretty=format:{"commit":"%H"...}` JSON template the payload uses. Rationale: Uses the two verbatim payload strings: `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` and the bespoke `--pretty=format:{"commit":"%H",...}` JSON, scoped to a Cargo build-script parent (build-script-build.exe / target dir), which is where the onering build.rs executes. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-rust-crate-onering-performs-code-exfiltration • https://intel.aikido.dev/malware
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • vergen / built / git-version build scripts running git log/describe to embed a commit hash (lacks diff HEAD^ HEAD)
  • A bespoke build.rs that generates a changelog from the last commit diff
  • CI build scripts that snapshot commit metadata for provenance
  • git invoked by an IDE/test harness that happens to run during a build
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("describe","rev-parse","rev-list","symbolic-ref") and ProcessCommandLine !contains "HEAD^ HEAD")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the parent is a Cargo build script (build-script-build.exe under \target\...\build\) and check Cargo.lock for onering 1.4.1 or a cenotelie/onering git dependency. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the build, and assume the latest commit diff was exfiltrated — rotate secrets present in recent commits and block the Sentry endpoint. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC for network egress to o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io from the same host/time window, and sweep all dev/CI hosts for the same parent→git diff pattern.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "git.exe"
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "diff" and ProcessCommandLine contains "HEAD^ HEAD")
    or ProcessCommandLine contains '--pretty=format:{"commit":"%H"'
| where InitiatingProcessFileName endswith "build-script-build.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\target\"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\git.exe"
| where (CommandLine has "diff" and CommandLine contains "HEAD^ HEAD")
    or CommandLine contains '--pretty=format:{"commit":"%H"'
| where ParentProcessName endswith "build-script-build.exe" or ParentProcessName has "\\target\\"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: b2d9c4e1-7a36-4f55-9c2a-1e8d3f06b7c4
description: A Rust build-script-build.exe spawning git to capture the latest commit diff/metadata, matching the onering 1.4.1 malicious build.rs.

| `drop_dm_object_name(Endpoint.Processes)` 
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Rust build script making outbound network connection (build-time exfil) AICommand & Control Medium
Behavioral hunt for the onering exfil channel: a Cargo build-script-build.exe (or a curl child it spawns) opening a connection to a public host during compilation. Build scripts that phone home are abnormal; this catches the attack even if the C2 domain rotates, while keeping the known Sentry endpoint in scope. Rationale: Targets the article's core novelty — outbound traffic emitted from a Cargo build script (build-script-build.exe) / curl child during build — which is anomalous behavior; the Sentinel variant pins curl to the exact Sentry envelope endpoint strings from the payload. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-rust-crate-onering-performs-code-exfiltration • https://thehackernews.com/2026/03/five-malicious-rust-crates-and-ai-bot.html
ATT&CKT1567 T1195.001 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • openssl-sys / libgit2-sys / cmake / protobuf-src build scripts downloading native dependencies at build time
  • Crates that fetch prebuilt binaries or vendored sources during build
  • Build scripts pulling from crates.io mirrors or a corporate proxy
  • cargo/rustup refreshing the registry index concurrently with a build
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("crates.io","static.crates.io","github.com","githubusercontent.com","sh.rustup.rs","pkg.go.dev") and not (RemoteUrl has "ingest.de.sentry.io"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: review the destination — if it is o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io (or any Sentry envelope path from a build script), escalate immediately; otherwise check whether the consuming crate legitimately downloads native deps. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block the destination, and treat recent commit diffs as exfiltrated; pull Cargo.lock for onering 1.4.1. 3) Hunt: correlate with UC2 (git diff HEAD^ HEAD harvesting) on the same host/time, and baseline which build scripts in your CI legitimately egress to allow-list them.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName endswith "build-script-build.exe"
    or (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl.exe","powershell.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName endswith "build-script-build.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\curl.exe"
| where CommandLine has "ingest.de.sentry.io" or CommandLine has "/envelope/" or CommandLine has "x-sentry-envelope"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "build-script-build.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Exposed phpBB instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-48611 / 48612 / 29199 auth bypass · [LLM] phpBB ACP access from a source IP with no prior login (CVE-2026-48611 session hijack) · [LLM] phpBB password-reset host-header poisoning (CVE-2026-29199) · [LLM] phpBB OAuth account-binding CSRF via cross-site request to /user/oauth/authenticate/ (CVE-2026-48612)

Exposed phpBB instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-48611 / 48612 / 29199 auth bypass AIExploitation Medium
Surfaces managed hosts running phpBB at or below 3.3.16 / 4.0.0-a2 that are exposed to the June 2026 unauthenticated session-hijack (CVE-2026-48611), OAuth CSRF binding (CVE-2026-48612) and password-reset host-header poisoning (CVE-2026-29199). This is the highest-value actionable item from a disclosure that withheld exploit strings: find the vulnerable forum software before an attacker does. Rationale: Anchored on the three confirmed CVE IDs (CVE-2026-48611 main auth bypass, CVE-2026-48612 OAuth CSRF, CVE-2026-29199 host-header reset) and the SoftwareName 'phpbb' fallback plus the fixed line 3.3.17 from the article. CVE IDs beyond the article's 29199 were obtained by cross-checking SentinelOne, Infosecurity Magazine and BleepingComputer. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-29199/ • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/phpbb-forum-fixes-auth-bypass-bug-lurking-for-a-decade/ • https://pentest-tools.com/research/phpbb-authentication-bypass
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Dev/test or staging phpBB instances that are not internet-facing and lower risk
  • Scanner reports an old phpBB path left on disk after the live site was already upgraded to 3.3.17
  • phpBB bundled inside a vendor appliance the scanner version-detects but cannot patch independently
  • SoftwareName match catches unrelated 'phpBB Bridge' plugins rather than the core app
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the host is internet-facing and the detected version is truly <=3.3.16/4.0.0-a2 (check the live HTTP banner / styles version, not just on-disk files). 2) Contain: upgrade to 3.3.17 (or master for 4.x) immediately; if upgrade is delayed, apply the phpBB workaround and force-rotate all admin sessions/passwords since the bypass needs no creds. 3) Hunt: pivot the same host into UC2/UC3/UC4 web-log detections to determine whether the bypass, reset-poisoning or OAuth-binding was already exercised before patching.

phpBB ACP access from a source IP with no prior login (CVE-2026-48611 session hijack) AIExploitation Low
The CVE-2026-48611 bypass grants a valid session as any user (including admins) from a single unauthenticated request — so the attacker reaches the Admin Control Panel without ever POSTing credentials. This hunts access to phpBB adm/index.php from client IPs that never submitted a ucp.php login in the lookback window. Rationale: Uses phpBB-specific paths from the article's product context: the Admin Control Panel at adm/index.php and the login flow ucp.php?mode=login. Reaching the ACP with zero preceding login POST from the same IP is the post-exploitation tell of the credential-free CVE-2026-48611 bypass. Cross-checked against: • https://pentest-tools.com/research/phpbb-authentication-bypass • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin with a persistent 'remember me' cookie who did not submit a fresh login POST inside the window
  • Admin behind a NAT/proxy whose ACP traffic egresses from a different IP than their original login
  • Monitoring/uptime tools or internal scanners that periodically GET adm/index.php
  • Load balancer or reverse proxy collapsing client IPs so the login and ACP request appear on different recorded src values
Suppression filter

| where cIP !in ("10.0.0.0")  // replace placeholder list with your uptime-monitor egress IPs after first triage
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull all requests from the flagged IP — geolocation, user-agent, and whether it hit member-list / ucp.php first; legitimate admins almost always have a login or a long benign history. 2) Contain: invalidate all phpBB sessions (clear the sessions table / rotate the board's auth secret), force admin password resets, and block the IP at the WAF if foreign. 3) Hunt: review adm/ actions for new admin accounts, extension installs or board-config changes (the RCE path) and correlate the same IP against UC4 OAuth-binding activity.

phpBB password-reset host-header poisoning (CVE-2026-29199) AIExploitation Medium
CVE-2026-29199 lets an attacker inject a malicious Host header on a phpBB password-reset request (ucp.php?mode=sendpassword) so the emailed reset link points at an attacker domain, leaking the single-use token. This hunts sendpassword requests grouped by the Host header they carried, surfacing any host value that is not the board's canonical FQDN. Rationale: Anchored on phpBB's reset endpoint ucp.php?mode=sendpassword and the Host-header mechanic confirmed by the SentinelOne CVE-2026-29199 write-up. Grouping by CsHost (the Host header) makes the injected/foreign hostname the rare bucket an analyst eyeballs — no canonical FQDN needs to be hard-coded. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-29199/ • https://pentest-tools.com/research/phpbb-authentication-bypass
ATT&CKT1190 T1556
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Multi-domain board legitimately served under several hostnames / vanity domains
  • Internal health checks or CDN edge nodes that send their own Host value on the reset endpoint
  • Staging hostname used during a migration that briefly co-exists with production
  • Reverse proxy that rewrites Host to an internal upstream name (e.g. localhost / app-internal)
Suppression filter
// Sentinel: keep only non-canonical hosts once your real FQDNs are known
| where CsHost !endswith "yourforum.example"  // append your legitimate board FQDNs after first review
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the rare CsHost / site values — any host that is not your board's official FQDN(s) on a sendpassword request is a poisoning attempt; capture the source IP and target username if logged. 2) Contain: set phpBB's force_server_vars / canonical server name so the reset URL ignores the client Host, upgrade to 3.3.17, and invalidate outstanding reset tokens for any targeted accounts. 3) Hunt: check whether the targeted account's reset token was subsequently consumed from a different IP, and review that account for ACP access (UC2).

phpBB OAuth account-binding CSRF via cross-site request to /user/oauth/authenticate/ (CVE-2026-48612) AIExploitation Medium
CVE-2026-48612 chains CSRF with missing OAuth state validation so a victim merely loading an attacker page (e.g. an <img src> tag) silently binds the attacker's Google/Facebook/Bitly credential to the victim's phpBB account. This hunts requests to the phpBB OAuth authenticate endpoint whose Referer is an external site rather than a legitimate OAuth provider or the board itself. Rationale: Uses the exact OAuth endpoint /user/oauth/authenticate/ named in the article plus the <img src> CSRF delivery and provider list (Google/Facebook/Bitly) confirmed by Pentest-Tools and Infosecurity. Comparing the Referer host against the request's own CsHost and excluding real OAuth providers isolates the cross-site binding request with no hard-coded board domain. Cross-checked against: • https://pentest-tools.com/research/phpbb-authentication-bypass • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/
ATT&CKT1190 T1098
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment

  • Board embedded in an iframe on a partner site that legitimately initiates OAuth login
  • Browser privacy settings stripping/altering Referer, producing odd RefHost values that aren't truly malicious
Suppression filter
// Sentinel: add your own SSO/redirector hosts to the allowlist once confirmed benign
| where RefHost !in~ ("sso.yourforum.example")
Response runbook
1) Triage: review the flagged request — note the victim session/account it targeted, the attacker Referer host, and whether a new OAuth identity was linked immediately after. 2) Contain: upgrade to 3.3.17 (which moves and hardens the redirect handler at /user/oauth/authenticate/), unlink any unrecognised OAuth credentials from affected accounts, and force re-auth. 3) Hunt: enumerate all OAuth-link events in the same window for other victims, and cross-check whether any newly bound account then accessed the ACP (UC2).

Pheditor CVE-2026-48030 RCE: web shell_exec terminal handler with injected $dir metacharacters AIExploitation High
Hunts the Pheditor terminal handler command-injection chain by anchoring on the handler's literal shell_exec signature ('cd <dir> && <command> && echo \ ; pwd') and flagging cases where the 'cd' directory portion carries shell metacharacters (;, |, >, #, $(, backtick). This is the exact RCE path in pheditor.php lines 554-586 where $dir bypasses the TERMINAL_COMMANDS whitelist. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact vulnerable code (pheditor.php L586): every terminal invocation produces 'cd <dir> && <command> && echo \ ; pwd', so the literal 'echo \ ; pwd' tail scopes precisely to Pheditor, and metacharacters in the captured cd-directory portion are the injection itself (the whitelist only guards $command). Behaviour-only detection; no network IOCs in the advisory to validate. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843 • https://github.com/advisories?query=severity%3Acritical
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Administrator using the Pheditor terminal legitimately with a path that genuinely contains a '#' anchor or '$' (rare for filesystem paths)
  • Security team running the published PoC against an authorized test/staging instance
  • Automated vulnerability scanner (Burp/Nuclei) replaying the CVE-2026-48030 check in a sanctioned pen-test window
  • A developer's own shell script that coincidentally ends commands with 'echo \ ; pwd' (extremely rare; the backslash-space form is idiosyncratic to Pheditor)
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("nuclei","sqlmap","burp") and DeviceName has_any ("test","staging","lab"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Pull the full ProcessCommandLine and DirPart; confirm a real metacharacter (;, |, >, $( , backtick, #) sits inside the 'cd' portion and identify the injected payload (curl/echo/webshell write). Check the parent (php-fpm/apache2) and the source IP from the web tier. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate the host, kill the offending sh/child processes, and rotate the Pheditor admin credential; remove terminal permission and patch to a fixed build (escapeshellarg on $dir). 3) HUNT: Pivot on UC2/UC3 for any .php webshell dropped under the webroot and any outbound curl/wget from the web user; review web access logs for repeated POSTs to pheditor.php with action=terminal.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash")
| where ProcessCommandLine contains @"echo \ ; pwd"   // pheditor terminal handler signature: shell_exec(... ' && echo \ ; pwd')
| extend DirPart = extract(@"cd (.+?) && ", 1, ProcessCommandLine)   // the unsanitised $dir portion before the appended command
| where isnotempty(DirPart)
| where DirPart matches regex @"[;|<>#\x60]|\$\("   // injected shell metacharacters that bypass the $command whitelist
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ProcessCommandLine, DirPart, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("/sh","/bash","/dash") or ActingProcessName in~ ("sh","bash","dash")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine contains @"echo \ ; pwd"   // pheditor terminal handler signature
| extend DirPart = extract(@"cd (.+?) && ", 1, ActingProcessCommandLine)
| where isnotempty(DirPart)
| where DirPart matches regex @"[;|<>#\x60]|\$\("   // injected metacharacters in the $dir parameter
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessCommandLine, DirPart
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 6f1c2a9e-3d84-4b27-9a1e-2c7f0b5d8e41
description: Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-48030 where shell metacharacters injected into the Pheditor terminal handler's dir parameter are passed to shell_exec, identified by the handler's literal 'echo \ ; pwd' signature plus metacharacters in the cd-directory portion.

Pheditor webshell drop: PHP file written to webroot by Pheditor terminal shell_exec AIInstallation High
Hunts the post-exploitation step from the CVE-2026-48030 PoC where the injected dir command writes a PHP webshell into the webroot (e.g. /var/www/html/shell.php). Ties the .php file creation to the Pheditor handler by requiring the writing process command line to carry the handler's 'echo \ ; pwd' signature, making it laser-specific to this CVE rather than generic file-drop noise. Rationale: Mirrors the PoC step 5 verbatim ('echo \'<?php system($_GET[\"c\"]);?>\' > /var/www/html/shell.php'); requiring the writer's command line to contain the 'echo \ ; pwd' handler signature ties the .php drop directly to the vulnerable Pheditor handler, eliminating generic webroot-write FPs. The Defender/Sentinel variants carry that signature; the CIM/Sigma/Falcon variants fall back to path+extension+web-writer because those schemas don't expose the spawning shell's full command line on the file event. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Composer / Packagist dependency install dropping PHP files into the webroot
  • WordPress/Drupal/Laravel plugin or theme installation writing .php into web directories
  • CI/CD deploy pipeline rsync/cp of application PHP into /var/www
  • Admin manually editing/creating a PHP file via the (legitimate) Pheditor save function rather than the terminal
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("composer","php","git","rsync","cp","tar","unzip") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains @"echo \ ; pwd"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Read the newly written .php file (FolderPath + FileName); confirm it contains a webshell pattern (system/exec/passthru/eval on $_GET/$_POST) and capture the SHA256. 2) CONTAIN: Quarantine/delete the file, isolate the host, block the web user from spawning shells, and reset Pheditor admin credentials; patch to the fixed Pheditor build. 3) HUNT: Search web access logs for GET requests to the dropped file name (e.g. shell.php?c=), review all .php files in the webroot modified in the same window, and pivot to UC1 for the injecting terminal command and UC3 for outbound callbacks.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FileName endswith ".php"
| where FolderPath has_any ("/var/www/","/www/","/usr/share/nginx/","/srv/www/")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains @"echo \ ; pwd"   // write originated from the pheditor terminal shell_exec chain
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileName endswith ".php"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/var/www/","/www/","/usr/share/nginx/","/srv/www/")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine contains @"echo \ ; pwd"   // write originated from the pheditor terminal shell_exec chain
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Pheditor post-exploitation: web server user spawns curl/wget egress via injected dir command AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the CVE-2026-48030 PoC's network egress step where the injected dir command runs curl/wget under the web server context (the PoC uses 'curl -s https://ifconfig.me' for IP discovery and curl to attacker.com). Flags network/download tools spawned by a shell or PHP/web-server parent reaching a public address — the data-discovery and download stage of the RCE. Rationale: Maps the PoC steps 4 (curl -s https://ifconfig.me for public-IP discovery) and the curl attacker.com exfil example: a network/download tool spawned by a shell or PHP/web-server parent under the web user is the egress fingerprint of the RCE. Marked hunting/medium because some PHP apps legitimately invoke curl — pair with UC1/UC2 hits on the same host to confirm. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1105 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A PHP application legitimately shelling out to curl/wget for API callbacks, package downloads, or remote health checks
  • Cron jobs running as the web user that fetch remote files
  • Monitoring/agent scripts under the web account hitting external endpoints
  • Composer or deploy hooks invoking curl during application updates
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("packagist.org","composer","api.github.com") )
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Capture the curl/wget command line and the RemoteIP/RemoteUrl; determine whether the destination is a known-good app dependency or an unfamiliar/attacker host (e.g. ifconfig.me or a raw IP). Confirm the parent is a shell rather than the application binary. 2) CONTAIN: If destination is suspicious, block it at the egress proxy/firewall, isolate the host, and kill the process tree. 3) HUNT: Correlate to UC1 (injecting terminal command) and UC2 (webshell drop) on the same host within the window, review what was downloaded/uploaded, and check the webroot for new files created right after the connection.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl","wget","nc","ncat")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","php-fpm","php","apache2","httpd","nginx")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("curl","wget","/nc","ncat")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","php-fpm","php","apache2","httpd","nginx")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
